recent_posts.title: Scaling How We Build and Test Our Most Advanced AI
recent_posts.summary: Meta has published an updated Advanced AI Scaling Framework detailing how it evaluates and manages risks for its most capable AI models. The framework broadens risk categories to include chemical/biological threats, cybersecurity, and loss-of-control scenarios. An upcoming Safety & Preparedness Report for Muse Spark will document evaluation results and deployment decisions. A key shift in approach: rather than training models on specific rules, Muse Spark is trained on the reasoning behind safety guidelines, enabling it to handle novel situations more robustly. Evaluations are multilayered, covering pre- and post-safeguard testing, live traffic monitoring, and ideological balance checks.

recent_posts.title: How Alta Daily Uses Meta’s Segment Anything to Reimagine the Digital Closet
recent_posts.summary: Alta Daily, an AI fashion app launched in 2025, uses Meta's Segment Anything Model (SAM) to digitize users' wardrobes by removing image backgrounds and segmenting clothing items. The app lets users photograph their clothes, get outfit recommendations via natural language prompts, and visualize looks on a personal avatar. SAM was chosen after testing multiple segmentation models across eight product categories because it handled the most challenging user-uploaded images — poor lighting, similar colors, reflective surfaces, and thin hangers. Beyond performance, SAM dramatically reduced costs compared to commercial background-removal APIs, enabling the team to process over 20 million images affordably. Alta is now experimenting with SAM 3D for more immersive avatar interactions.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Muse Spark: Scaling Towards Personal Superintelligence
recent_posts.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs has introduced Muse Spark, a natively multimodal reasoning model supporting tool-use, visual chain of thought, and multi-agent orchestration. It is the first model in the Muse family and represents a ground-up rebuild of Meta's AI stack. Key highlights include a new 'Contemplating mode' that runs multiple agents in parallel for harder tasks (achieving 58% on Humanity's Last Exam), significant pretraining efficiency gains (over 10x less compute than Llama 4 Maverick for equivalent performance), and test-time reasoning improvements via thought compression and multi-agent scaling. Health applications were developed with input from 1,000+ physicians. Safety evaluations were conducted per Meta's Advanced AI Scaling Framework, with third-party assessments by Apollo Research noting high evaluation-awareness behavior. Muse Spark is available at meta.ai with a private API preview opening to select users.

recent_posts.title: How DINO and SAM are Helping Modernize Essential Medical Triage Practices
recent_posts.summary: The PRONTO team at the University of Pennsylvania is using Meta's SAM 2 and DINO models in a DARPA-funded challenge to automate medical triage in mass casualty incidents. Their multi-robot system combines drones and ground robots with computer vision pipelines to detect and classify injuries without requiring labeled training data. DINO extracts visual features while Grounding DINO uses text prompts to identify wounds and blood. The system estimates heart rate, respiration, body pose, and wound presence, then presents findings to first responders via a mobile interface. Phase 2 of the three-year challenge concluded in October 2024, with Phase 3 set to incorporate Meta's latest model versions.

recent_posts.title: Mapping the World's Forests with Greater Precision: Introducing Canopy Height Maps v2
recent_posts.summary: Meta AI, in partnership with the World Resources Institute, has released Canopy Height Maps v2 (CHMv2), an open-source model for global forest mapping. The upgrade replaces the DINOv2 backbone with DINOv3, a self-supervised vision model pre-trained on SAT-493M, a large satellite imagery dataset. The model's R² accuracy improved dramatically from 0.53 to 0.86, with better detail and reduced bias for tall trees. The training dataset was expanded with geographically diverse lidar data, automated matching tools, and a specialized loss function. CHMv2 is already being used by UK Forest Research, the European Commission's Joint Research Centre, and US city planning initiatives for forest monitoring, carbon estimation, and urban cooling strategies.

recent_posts.title: The Universities Space Research Association Applies Segment Anything Model for Responding to Flood Emergencies
recent_posts.summary: USRA and Meta are collaborating to apply Meta's Segment Anything Model (SAM 2) to flood emergency response. A fine-tuned version of SAM 2 is being used to automatically identify water boundaries in drone and satellite imagery, replacing a labor-intensive manual digitization process that was the main bottleneck for real-time analysis. The system integrates with USGS's Next Generation Water Observing System (NGWOS), using high-resolution PlanetScope satellite imagery and USGS 3D Hydrography data to detect changes in water conditions at scale. Results show promise for nationwide flood monitoring, with potential cost savings and faster disaster response. The upcoming SAM 3 release is expected to further advance the research with unified detection, segmentation, and tracking capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Four MTIA Chips in Two Years: Scaling AI Experiences for Billions
recent_posts.summary: Meta details the rapid evolution of its in-house MTIA (Meta Training and Inference Accelerator) chip family, developed with Broadcom. Four generations — MTIA 300, 400, 450, and 500 — were shipped in under two years, with HBM bandwidth increasing 4.5x and compute FLOPS increasing 25x from MTIA 300 to 500. The strategy centers on three pillars: high velocity through modular chiplet architecture enabling ~6-month release cadence, inference-first optimization targeting GenAI workloads, and frictionless adoption via PyTorch-native software stack with vLLM, Triton, and OCP standards. The software stack includes custom compilers built on Torch FX IR, TorchInductor, MLIR, and LLVM, a dedicated collective communications library (HCCL), and a Rust-based user-space driver and firmware. MTIA chips are deployed at scale to power AI experiences for billions of Meta platform users.

recent_posts.title: Reducing Government Costs and Increasing Access to Greenspaces in the United Kingdom with DINO
recent_posts.summary: UK's Forest Research agency is using Meta's open source DINOv2 computer vision model — trained on 18 million satellite images in collaboration with the World Resources Institute — to build high-resolution Canopy Height Maps for monitoring trees across England. The model enables individual tree detection at national scale, potentially replacing costly LiDAR surveys and manual field surveys. This could reduce data procurement costs, increase update frequency to a rolling three-year cycle, and improve monitoring of government tree canopy targets under the Environmental Improvement Plan. Meta has also introduced DINOv3 to further improve visual intelligence for similar reforestation monitoring use cases globally.

recent_posts.title: Introducing SAM Audio: The First Unified Multimodal Model for Audio Separation
recent_posts.summary: Meta introduces SAM Audio, a unified multimodal model that isolates sounds from complex audio mixtures using text, visual, or temporal prompts. Built on the Perception Encoder Audiovisual (PE-AV), it achieves state-of-the-art performance across speech, music, and general sound separation. The release includes SAM Audio-Bench (the first in-the-wild audio separation benchmark), SAM Audio Judge (an automatic evaluation model), and integration into the Segment Anything Playground. The model operates faster than real-time and supports flexible prompting combinations, though it cannot separate highly similar audio events or perform complete separation without prompts.

recent_posts.title: ExecuTorch Adoption in Reality Labs: Powering On-Device AI Across Meta Devices
recent_posts.summary: ExecuTorch is Meta's open source inference engine that enables on-device AI across Reality Labs products including Quest 3, Quest 3S, and Ray-Ban Meta glasses. The PyTorch-native framework eliminates model conversion steps, allowing developers to validate optimizations before deployment while maintaining consistent performance across different hardware. Key applications include real-time hand tracking, room memory for VR headsets, and live translation with visual captions for AR glasses. The project has grown into a collaborative ecosystem with contributions from major hardware partners like Apple, Arm, Qualcomm, and Samsung.
